Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Printed under STAR QUESTIONS PLUS (pp.52-53), and the LAQ chapter cross-references it ("For Calvin Cycle 'Q' Refer P.No: 52(168)"), so the book treats it as major content: the printed answer runs two pages with a full cycle diagram. FLAGGED FOR FOUNDER REVIEW: that is Section-C-grade material, but the 2022 blue print gives Photosynthesis 6 marks with NO Section-C slot, and the book prints it outside every LAQ chapter. It is therefore authored at 4 marks and NO 8-mark form is invented — the same discipline the junior botany track used for Section-C-grade content the book does not source as an LAQ. Examiner audit revision (2026-09-05): the regeneration ATP line now says one ATP per RuBP and six in all, because the step is written in the six-turn frame (twelve G-3-P, six RuBP) where a bare "one more ATP" gave 13 ATP per six CO2 instead of 18.

insider_note: Three phases, in order, with the number of carbons at each step. Carbon fixation, reduction, regeneration — an answer that names all three in order has most of the marks already.

steps.label: What the Calvin cycle is
steps.margin_note: Definition, site, alternative names, the three phase names. Six lines.
lines: The Calvin cycle is the cyclic process in which
carbon dioxide from the air is converted into
sugar.
It occurs in the STROMA of the chloroplast.
It is the dark reaction, or C3 pathway.
It has THREE phases: carbon fixation,
reduction and regeneration.
steps.why: Naming the three phases in the first step turns the rest of the answer into three labelled paragraphs, which is how the marks are actually split.
common_mistakes: Saying the Calvin cycle happens in the grana. It happens in the STROMA.
Calling it the light reaction. It is the DARK reaction.
steps.memory_tip: Stroma, three phases: fix, reduce, regenerate.

steps.label: Carbon fixation phase
steps.margin_note: Acceptor, enzyme, equation, first product. The word bisphosphate matters.
lines: 1. CARBON FIXATION:
CO2 combines with the 5-carbon compound RuBP
(ribulose 1,5-bisphosphate).
The enzyme is RuBisCO.
PGA is the first stable product, so this is
called the C3 pathway.
steps.why: A 5-carbon acceptor plus a 1-carbon gas gives a 6-carbon compound that splits at once into two 3-carbon molecules, which is why twelve PGA come from six RuBP.
common_mistakes: Naming PEP as the acceptor. PEP is the C4 acceptor; RuBP is the C3 acceptor.
Writing RuBP as ribulose biphosphate. It is BISphosphate — two separate phosphates.
steps.memory_tip: Five carbons plus one makes six, which splits into two threes.

steps.label: Reduction phase
steps.margin_note: Both steps with their equations, then the 3-and-2 ratio. The ratio is often asked alone.
lines: 2. REDUCTION:
A two step reaction that forms trioses (G-3-P).
Step 1 uses ATP:
Step 2 uses NADPH:
Fixing ONE CO2 needs 3 ATP and 2 NADPH.
steps.why: This is where the ATP and NADPH made in the light reaction are actually spent, which is what links the dark reaction back to the light one.
common_mistakes: Saying the reduction phase uses NADH. It uses NADPH.
Giving the wrong ratio. Per carbon dioxide fixed it is 3 ATP and 2 NADPH.
steps.memory_tip: Three ATP and two NADPH buy one carbon.

steps.label: Regeneration phase
steps.margin_note: Say what is rebuilt, what it costs, and how much product actually leaves.

lines.text: RuBP is rebuilt, so the cycle can run again

lines: 3. REGENERATION:
The CO2 acceptor RuBP is formed again, so the
cycle can continue.
This needs ONE more ATP for phosphorylation,
one per RuBP, so SIX in all.
Of the twelve G-3-P formed, TEN are used to
rebuild six RuBP; the other TWO leave the cycle
as sugar.
steps.why: The cycle only continues because most of its own product is spent rebuilding the acceptor, which is why so little sugar leaves per turn.
common_mistakes: Saying all the G-3-P becomes sugar. Most of it is used to REBUILD RuBP.
Leaving out the extra ATP. Regeneration costs one more ATP per RuBP.
steps.memory_tip: Ten back into the cycle, two out as sugar.

steps.label: Diagram — the Calvin cycle
steps.margin_note: No diagram mark — the question says explain. Draw it anyway: the ring makes the regeneration mark almost self-explaining.

elements.caption: Step 1 — carbon fixation: CO2 joins RuBP
Step 2 — reduction: ATP and NADPH make triose phosphate
Step 3 — regeneration: RuBP is built again
Step 4 — the sugar that leaves the cycle

steps.why: The three phases only make sense as a ring: the compound the cycle ends by rebuilding is the same one it started by using, and a straight-line drawing hides that.
common_mistakes: Drawing the cycle as a straight chain. It is a CYCLE; RuBP is regenerated.
Drawing the sugar leaving from RuBP. Sugar leaves from the TRIOSE PHOSPHATE stage.
Putting the ATP input only at reduction. Regeneration needs ATP as well.
steps.memory_tip: One ring, three numbered arcs, one arrow out.
